title: Marked mapping-simplex presentations determine coherent transport
statement:
Use [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], and the straightening equivalence $\operatorname{St}_S:\operatorname{coCart}(S)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(S,\mathrm{Cat}_\infty)$ of [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Work in a common containing universe. Let $C$ be a small ordinary category and $D:C\to\mathsf{sSet}$ a strict functor with quasicategory values. Define $R_C(D)$ by the following simplices: an $n$-simplex consists of $\sigma:[n]\to C$ and maps $t_J:\Delta^J\to D(\sigma(\max J))$ for every nonempty $J\subseteq[n]$, with
$$t_J|_{\Delta^I}=D(\sigma(\max I)\to\sigma(\max J))t_I\quad(\varnothing\ne I\subseteq J).$$
An operator $\theta:[m]\to[n]$ sends these data to $\sigma\theta$ and $t'_J=t_{\theta(J)}\circ\Delta(\theta|_J)$. Projection to $\sigma$ defines $r:R_C(D)\to N(C)$. There is a simplicial map $i_D:G_C(D)\to R_C(D)$ over $N(C)$ given on $(\sigma,\tau)$ by $t_J=D(\sigma(0)\to\sigma(\max J))(\tau|_{\Delta^J})$.

Then $r$ is a cocartesian fibration classified by the coherent diagram $D$, with fibres $D(c)$. An edge over $f:c\to d$ is $r$-cocartesian precisely when its edge in $D(d)$ is an equivalence. For every cocartesian fibration $q:Q\to N(C)$, precomposition with $i_D$ is an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{cocart}}_{/N(C)}(R_C(D),Q)\xrightarrow{\simeq}\operatorname{Fun}^{\mathrm{mark}}_{/N(C)}(G_C(D),Q).$$
Each side is the full subcategory of the simplicial mapping object over $N(C)$ on maps preserving the indicated edges: all cocartesian edges on the left and the marked edges of $G_C(D)$ on the right; its higher simplices are arbitrary transformations over the base. The comparison is compatible with postcomposition by cocartesian maps, with strict transformations of $D$, and with pullback along $N(u)$ for functors $u:C'\to C$.

Consequently a strict presentation $\varphi:G_C(D)\to Q$ determines an equivalence $\alpha_\varphi:D\simeq\operatorname{St}_{N(C)}(q)$ whose component at $c$ is the fibre equivalence $\varphi_c:D(c)\to Q_c$ and whose transport edges are $\varphi(f,s_0x)$. This identification is coherent over all simplices. For another strict presentation $\varphi'$ of $q':Q'\to N(C)$, a strict transformation $\eta:D\to D'$ and a cocartesian map $g:Q\to Q'$ with $g\varphi=\varphi'G_C(\eta)$, there is a coherent natural equivalence
$$\operatorname{St}(g)\alpha_\varphi\simeq\alpha_{\varphi'}\eta.$$
These identifications commute coherently with pullback in $C$.

source.place: Definition 3.2.5.2, Remarks 3.2.5.4 and 3.2.5.7, and Proposition 3.2.5.21 for the relative nerve. The marked mapping-simplex comparison is the global form of Proposition 3.2.2.14 (cocartesian dual), with the relative-nerve comparison of §3.2.5. Kerodon Proposition 5.6.4.8 (Subsection tag 0279) compares the weighted nerve with the category of elements; Definition 5.6.5.1 (028V) defines transport representation. The general marked mapping-object and naturality formulation is an agent-formulated foundation, not quoted verbatim as a proposition in HTT. Read online; WANTED: archived HTT and Kerodon.
